headline: Chinese robot maker Leju and parts maker Zhaofeng now run 15 humanoid robots on a car-parts loading line, with a reported 98% success rate but slower work than people.
score_reason: Real factory deployment with numbers, but the figures are company-supplied and the robots are still about two and a half times slower than a skilled worker.
importance_line: Factory workers and parts makers are affected if humanoids reach human speed, but the success rate is the company's figure and the robots are not yet fast enough for wider use.
summary: Pandaily reports, citing Securities Times, that Leju Robotics and auto parts maker Zhaofeng have run 15 humanoid robots on a parts loading line near Hangzhou for more than two months, about 1,000 hours, with a loading success rate of 98% according to a Zhaofeng representative. A loading cycle still takes under 40 seconds against about 15 for a skilled worker, and Zhaofeng's chairman says humanoids need to reach about 15 seconds, which he expects to take six months to a year.
notes: Presented 15 Oct 2026; figures are company claims relayed by Pandaily.
